title: Visualizations of Polarization-Induced Atomic Vibrational Anisotropies Using Momentum Selective Vibrational Spectroscopy
content: Studying vibrational anisotropies for individual phonon modes is essential for understanding intriguing optical, thermal, and mechanical phenomena in crystalline materials. At the atomic level, vibrations of atoms, known as thermal ellipsoids, exhibit significant anisotropies due to local symmetries and bonding configurations. The vibrational anisotropies of distinct elements are traditionally characterized by diffraction methods, which all encountered critical shortcomings of insufficient spatial and energy resolutions [1]. The thermal ellipsoids averaged across the entire phonon spectrum obscure the linkage between atomic vibrations and specific material responses associated with acoustic or optical phonon modes. Thanks to the groundbreaking innovation of new-type monochromator and spectrometer, we can routinely detect nanoscale phonon spectrum and dynamics using ultrahigh energy resolution electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) in advanced scanning transmission electron microscopes (STEMs) [2, 3]. Recently, we developed a momentum-selective dark-field vibrational EELS approach with controlled momentum exchanges to capture the atomically resolved vibrational spectra with the capabilities of differentiating elements and crystalline positions [4]. Here, we applied this new tool to distinguish the altered vibrational anisotropies of apical and equatorial oxygen atoms in a non-centrosymmetric BaTiO3 (BTO).
